chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ismail ibn Ammar, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who broadcasts an immorality is like its initiator, and the one who rebukes a believer with something will not die until he commits it.'

key_terms.يَرْكَبَهُ: he commits it / it overtakes him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of publicizing a sin or accusing a believer of a specific fault?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the legal and spiritual principle that publicizing a hidden sin (idha' al-fahisha) elevates the broadcaster to the status of the sinner, a concept often linked to Surah An-Nur. The second part warns against specific accusation (ta'yeer), suggesting a divine retribution where the accuser may eventually succumb to the very fault they highlighted, reflecting the Shia emphasis on guarding the community's honor.
